title: SDK: improve retry/backoff defaults + typed errors (onboarding parity) and refresh docs examples
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: Python SDK now ships onboarding-aligned retry defaults (exponential backoff w/ jitter, Retry-After support) and improved typed errors (Auth/RateLimit/Timeout/Connection). Examples used by docs updated to demonstrate timeouts + safe retries.
body:
Summary: This PR updates the Python SDK retry/backoff behavior and error typing to match the Guided Onboarding + “First production launch” guidance. It also refreshes the code snippets/examples referenced by docs/quickstarts so users see the canonical patterns (timeouts, request IDs, safe retries, and streaming caveats).

Motivation / context: We’ve seen onboarding tickets where users either (a) don’t retry transient failures and get flaky demos, or (b) retry everything (including auth / malformed requests) and end up with confusing loops. Support also flagged confusion between “401 wrong key environment” vs “network/timeout”. This PR standardizes defaults and makes errors actionable by type.

User-visible changes (behavior): - Default retries for non-streaming requests: enabled with max_retries=2 (configurable), exponential backoff with full jitter, capped at 8s, base 0.5s. - 429 handling: retries include Retry-After header support (seconds or HTTP date). If Retry-After is present, it wins over exponential backoff (bounded by max_backoff). - 5xx handling: retries on 500/502/503/504 by default. - 408/409 handling: retries on request timeout (408) and conflict (409) only when the request is marked idempotent; by default the SDK treats standard POST /responses as non-idempotent unless an idempotency_key is supplied. - 4xx handling: no retries on 400/401/403/404/422. - Streaming: by default we do not automatically retry a dropped stream because it can duplicate tokens/side effects; we surface a typed StreamingInterruptedError with guidance to re-issue the request with your own app-level safeguards.

User-visible changes (errors): Introduces typed exceptions with consistent fields: - RedwoodError (base): message, request_id, status_code (optional), response_body (redacted/limited), cause (optional) - AuthenticationError (401/403) - RateLimitError (429) incl. retry_after_seconds (optional) - InvalidRequestError (400/404/422) - TimeoutError (408, socket timeouts) - APIConnectionError (DNS/TLS/reset) - APIError (5xx + unknown)

Also: All raised errors now attempt to include request_id from response headers (x-redwood-request-id) and from client-generated request IDs when available.

Docs/examples updates: - examples/quickstart.py updated to show: client init, setting timeouts, handling RateLimitError with backoff, and printing request_id in exception handling. - examples/streaming.py updated to show robust stream consumption and handling StreamingInterruptedError without auto-retry. - These examples are the ones referenced by the docs site snippets (ENG-23121/ENG-23122 alignment).

Implementation details: - New retry policy lives in redwood_sdk/_retry.py (pure function + small class wrapper) to keep client.py smaller. - Retries are applied at the transport boundary (requests.Session send wrapper) so we cover both JSON and SSE setup, but we explicitly skip replays once a stream has begun emitting tokens. - Dedupe: when a request is retried and the user provided an idempotency_key, we keep the same key across attempts.

Files / areas changed: - redwood_sdk/client.py: wire retry + timeout defaults, propagate request_id, add config knobs. - redwood_sdk/errors.py: typed error classes + mapping from status codes. - redwood_sdk/_retry.py: exponential backoff + Retry-After parsing and jitter. - redwood_sdk/transport.py: centralized send() with retry loop + classification of failures. - examples/quickstart.py, examples/streaming.py: updated canonical snippets. - tests/: new unit tests for retry classification + Retry-After + error typing.

Testing: - Unit tests added for: classification matrix (status codes), retry-after parsing, jitter bounds (deterministic via seeded RNG), and ensuring we don’t retry on 401/422. - Integration-ish tests (mocked responses) verifying request_id propagation and that RateLimitError surfaces retry_after_seconds.

Rollout notes / compatibility: - This is intended to be backwards compatible: existing code catching Exception will continue to work; however, users who were checking string contents of errors may see different messages. - No API surface removed. We added optional kwargs (max_retries, timeout, idempotency_key) and new exception types.

Follow-ups: - Consider exposing a structured hook for metrics/tracing (on_retry callback) once telemetry contracts for onboarding are finalized. - Consider adding a short doc note about when to opt into streaming retries (app-specific) vs relying on SDK.

Links: - Linear: ENG-23121, ENG-23122 - Related onboarding work: Console checklist step for retries/timeouts (in “First production launch”) - Support references: SUP-9244 (wrong key env 401), SUP-9210 (streaming disconnect confusion)

Checklist: - [x] Added tests - [x] Updated examples referenced by docs - [x] Verified no prompt/content logged in exceptions (messages capped and redacted) - [x] Changelog note drafted
commits: sdk(py): add retry policy module + Retry-After parsing
sdk(py): introduce typed errors and map status codes
sdk(py): wire retry/timeouts into transport layer
examples: update quickstart + streaming to canonical onboarding patterns
tests: coverage for retry classification and error typing
review_conversation: Monica Patel: Can we confirm we’re not retrying any 4xx besides 429, and that the default max_retries is conservative? Also please add a short note in the docstring about streaming not being auto-retried.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Confirmed: only 429 + selected 5xx + timeouts are retried. Default max_retries=2. Added docstring + error message guidance for StreamingInterruptedError.
Amara Diallo: Retry-After parsing looks good. Please cap absurd Retry-After values (e.g., 1h) and ensure we include request_id in the raised RateLimitError for support debugging.
Ibrahim Khan (author): Added max_backoff cap (default 8s) applied to Retry-After, and ensured request_id is parsed from headers into all RedwoodError subclasses.

Wei Chen: The quickstart snippet should show the exact exception names we want in docs (RateLimitError, AuthenticationError). Also please keep the snippet minimal and avoid custom sleep loops in the main path.

Ibrahim Khan (author): Updated examples/quickstart.py to demonstrate catching RateLimitError and AuthenticationError, and moved the more advanced retry customization into a commented “production” section.
Monica Patel: One more request—ensure we don’t include raw response bodies in exception messages (redaction / size cap).
Ibrahim Khan (author): Done. response_body is capped to 2KB, redacts known fields, and is not included in __str__ by default.
notes: CI initially failed due to a flaky timing-based jitter assertion; updated to use seeded RNG and assert bounds only, then re-ran checks successfully.
